etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Middle English mayntenen, from Old French maintenir, from Late Latin manūteneō, manūtenēre (“I support”), from Latin manū (“with/in/by the hand”, ablative of manus) + tenēre (“to hold”).
senses: To keep up; to preserve; to uphold (a state, condition etc.). [from 14th c.]
To declare or affirm (a clause) to be true; to assert. [from 15th c.]
